title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic refractory body-centered-cubic high-entropy alloy (e.g. Mo–Nb–Ta–W–V or a similar five-component system)
recollection.intervention: Controlled thermal annealing at intermediate temperatures to induce chemical short-range order (CSRO) without triggering long-range phase separation
recollection.structure: Retention of single-phase BCC matrix containing nanoscale clusters of preferential atom pairs/triplets (CSRO domains) a few nanometers across
recollection.mechanism: Local ordering reduces mass-disorder and force-constant fluctuations by grouping like atoms, thereby decreasing phonon scattering and extending phonon mean free paths
recollection.results: Room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity increased by roughly 30% compared with the fully random alloy (from ~8 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ to ~11 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹); inelastic scattering experiments confirmed a 20–40% reduction in phonon linewidths for mid-frequency modes

score.note: The recollection substitutes thermal annealing for the Monte Carlo-induced SRO and identifies the wrong alloy family. It generically recalls nanoscale ordering in a BCC matrix but misses the specific B2-like HfTi/TiZr clusters and percolating pathways. The reduced-scattering explanation overlaps partly with the actual reduction in lattice distortion, but it omits the key percolation mechanism and misstates the atomic-ordering basis. The claimed ~30% increase, absolute conductivities, and linewidth changes do not match the reported ~12% increase.
